marks.description: A pair of small, pinprick scars on the forearm, where James drank Seraphina's corrupted blood. On cold nights, they burn; under moonlight, they glow faintly.
marks.concealment: Always hidden beneath gauntlets or heavy fur cuffs.

marks.description: Red eyes that bleed when crying

memories.name: Memory 1
memories.description: Your mortal life — broad overview of who you were before the nights began.
experiences: I was born into silk and sycophants in the misty highlands around 1050 AD — surrounded by those who flattered every whim, I grew arrogant in the knowledge that the world would bend or break for me, not the other way round.

memories.name: Memory 2
memories.description: A memory in your immortal life — holds one Experience (two selected traits woven together).
experiences: The banner of a rival house burned over the borderlands, and in the reek of smoke and blood your swordsmanship became the final word your enemies heard; you felt nothing but the old warmth of the blade doing what it was forged to do.

memories.name: Memory 3
memories.description: A memory in your immortal life — holds one Experience (two selected traits woven together).
experiences: Elspeth begged you to spare the villages your raids had reduced to ghosts, and you let her have that mercy — not for her sake, but because her voice was one thread in the tapestry of cruelty you had learned to love that still held your hand.

memories.name: Memory 4
memories.description: A memory in your immortal life — holds one Experience (two selected traits woven together).
experiences: Jack's own retinue deserted him when your tactics stripped his lands bare, and you found his last letter burning in the hearth before you had to answer his challenge; the gem in your blade drank the light one last time.

memories.name: Memory 5
memories.description: A memory in your immortal life — holds one Experience (two selected traits woven together).
experiences: Sister Seraphina pressed the cold of the borderlands into your mouth and tasted the emptiness beneath your pride — there, where the leprosy ate her like slow fire, you found a hunger that would outlast the centuries, and you drank until the world sharpened and the wind in the highlands learned your name.
